briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Operators Get a Legal Fast-Track and a Governor's Race Ally, While National Cannabis and Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's fight over the 24% wholesale tax is finally moving toward resolution, with the state Supreme Court fast-tracking the case and a leading gubernatorial candidate pledging repeal. Nationally, courts and the DEA itself are reinforcing the rescheduling shift while Compass Pathways' psilocybin program keeps hitting milestones toward FDA approval.

local.text: MiCIA endorses GOP's John James for tax repeal — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association officially endorsed Republican gubernatorial candidate John James, citing his commitment to repealing the controversial 24% wholesale tax imposed on marijuana businesses last year.

Michigan Supreme Court fast-tracks wholesale-tax case — The Michigan Supreme Court recently stepped in, ordering an expedited review to settle the matter quickly due to the high stakes for the industry.
Bipartisan bill takes aim at the wholesale tax — The 24% wholesale tax is driving closures, spurring an HB 6224 repeal push in Lansing.

Muskegon dispensary-restaurant targets fall opening — Fields Cannary is targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow, pushing the hospitality-forward format further than most Michigan dispensaries have gone.
Michigan holds onto No. 2 market status — The state posted $263.5 million in August sales and moved over 30.4 million units, proof that demand keeps volume strong even as dollar totals soften.

national.text: Federal court upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III move — The D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge from rescheduling opponents on Sept. 9, leaving the DOJ's order reclassifying state-licensed medical marijuana in effect.

DEA itself argues weed no longer fits Schedule I — In its own final brief, the DEA argued marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, with a recommendation from the hearing judge still pending.

Compass Pathways touts durable data, soaring stock — The company highlighted durable Phase III data and a broad commercial build-out at an industry summit, with shares delivering a 193% return over the past year.

States say DEA is stonewalling on rescheduling rollout — California's cannabis regulator said the DEA hasn't shown any interest in providing states guidance on the rescheduling move, even as it seeks more information on the state's medical program.

Compass lines up training partner ahead of FDA call — Compass Pathways selected Fluence to design post-approval provider training for COMP360, signaling industry focus on workforce readiness ahead of a potential FDA approval.
